LESSON: WATER HARDNESS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 1.3: Water hardness
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Water hardness, part of Mixtures, Elements and Compounds in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we soften hard water? 2. Why is hard water preferred for drinking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Water hardness together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: The learner learns new methods of softening water as they apply methods of softening hard water in day

to day life.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner learns ways of reducing soap wastage as they relate the lathering ability

of water to hardness and softness of water.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner plays a role when carrying out experiments on softening hard water.

● Respect: The learner gives others an opportunity to air their views as they discuss in a group the differences between hard and

soft water.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Financial literacy: The learner practices how to save on soap by using soft water for laundry.

Link to other subjects:

Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner relates the uses soft water in laundry work.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology such as adapted keyboard, screen readers and screen magnifiers, print materials in

appropriate font and colour contrast and braille materials and equipment.
